candidate.footnote_text: The terse Hebrew request is difficult. 'Lot' is supplied from the selection scene; another interpretation is 'Answer honestly.' The Rahlfs–Hanhart Greek text has a longer prayer asking why God has not answered and distinguishing guilt in Saul or Jonathan from guilt in the people. Its requests are commonly interpreted in terms of Urim and Thummim; these are not preserved Hebrew words in 4Q52 fragment 2, whose reconstruction and identification with this passage are disputed.
candidate.lexical_rationale: The pointed form can express completeness or blamelessness and can function substantivally; Amos 5:10 also supports truth-conforming content. The selection scene in verses 40–42 supplies 'lot', not the word itself. 'Answer honestly' is an interpretive alternative, not an established superior rendering or a word-for-word gloss. BDB's target cross-reference proposes Thummim instead of the pointed form and must not be cited as direct approval of the retained English. Source prayer length and Greek interpretation remain separate unresolved questions. The historical HALOT label is retained; no fresh HALOT consultation is claimed.
